describe: Desktop light onboarding interest-picker screen. A curly-haired boy in a blue jacket with an orange backpack stands at the left on a glowing circular floor platform, pointing up and to the right; the small white-and-blue robot Nova stands beside him with one arm raised and a finger up, their bodies touching, so both are captured in ONE character box (hair top y=240, shoe/foot bottom y=767, backpack/shoe left x=105, robot's raised hand right x=495). The backdrop is an illustrated pastel futuristic city skyline with translucent domes and towers, a lilac starfield sky with floating ringed planets, and a luminous reflective floor - not flat. UI to erase: the Kidsverse+ logo lockup top-left, the circular back chevron and the segmented step-progress bar with its planet marker across the top, the English language chip top-right, the 'What makes you curious?' headline (own box) and its subtitle line, the boy's speech bubble including its downward tail (tail tip at y=247), the cluster of four translucent floating interest cards (planet, faint blank card, elephant, art palette) beside his pointing hand, the eight-card interest grid in two rows of four with check badges and labels (row boxes made to overlap so no card glow or gutter fragment survives), the '3 selected' hint panel and the CONTINUE gradient button at the bottom, and the bottom-left Back pill. There is no bottom navigation dock on this screen. The floating cards sit inside the character bounding box, so they are also listed as erase rectangles, carefully routed around the boy's pointing fist (right edge x=361), the robot's antenna ball (x 365-397, y 450-485), the robot's head rim (right edge x=443, y 495-560) and the robot's raised hand (top y=533) so none of the character is wiped; a small erase rectangle also removes the speech-bubble tail tip that falls inside the top of the character box.
